name: Freshly reconnected account, one salary sighting: not credited, the mortgage is covered by a move (G359)

expected.notes: Re-derived for G360 with the pay on the 1st (calendar month) and the salary mid-period. Today is Thu 8 Oct 2026, payday Sun 1 Nov, 24 days away; the window is strictly before payday. The account was reconnected recently, so nothing is confirmed. Balances: Barclays 200 + Starling 2,000 = 2,200 pooled. The salary 3,000 expected Thu 15 Oct has a single sighting. A steady salary needs two, a reliable one three, so it is NOT credited to Barclays in any per-account walk. The mortgage 1,100 leaves Barclays on Fri 16 Oct. Left to spend is a pooled figure and the pool counts every expected income: 2,200, day 7 + 3,000 = 5,200, day 8 - 1,100 = 4,100, lowest point the opening 2,200, so Left to spend 2,200. Barclays walk (salary not credited): 200 - 1,100 = -900: after payments -900 and low point -900, so the verdict is short. At risk count is 1: the badge walks the account on its own balance and the mortgage (a commitment) takes it below zero (200 < 1,100). It counts the short walk, not the outcome; the cover move below is what resolves it. The cover plan sizes the move as the shortfall 900 rounded up to the next 5 (900) plus 10 = 910, taken from Starling, which can spare it (2,000, keeping at least 10). Spend from: Barclays is -900, shown as 0 (floored); Starling is 2,000 less the 910 its own live move card reserves = 1,090, under the pool of 2,200. The period is on day 8 (1 Oct is day 1), so there is no payday plan (companion.py:2558, days_into_period <= 3). Client walk (G372): the salary has no credit_basis, so the walk does not credit it either: Barclays walks 200 - 1,100 = -900 and reads short, matching the server (the walk previously credited the 3,000 and read 2,100 covered). G414 allocation: Barclays has 910.00 suggested in minus its 900.00 deficit = 10.00 conditional availability. Starling 1,090.00 plus Barclays 10.00 safely allocates 1,100.00; the other 1,100.00 of pooled 2,200.00 depends on an uncredited single income sighting and stays explicitly unallocated. G436 (Kevin 2026-11-07), which supersedes the Left to spend and Spend from figures worked above where they differ: Left to spend is the sum of each account's own lowest point plus income no account credits, on its own line. Barclays 200 - 1,100 = -900 and Starling 2,000, so 1,100 across the accounts (the 910 suggested move nets to zero: Barclays -900 + 910 = 10, Starling 2,000 - 910 = 1,090). The single-sighting 3,000 salary is credited to no account walk, but the pooled walk counted it: without it the pooled low point is 2,200 - 1,100 = 1,100, with it (day 7, before the mortgage on day 8) 2,200, so it adds 1,100. That stays in Left to spend as its own line (income not tied to one account): 1,100 + 1,100 = 2,200, unchanged. Whether such income should count is a decision for Kevin.
